say.t: Spring, 2016. A hundred-odd desks in the office, not one of them empty.
On the whiteboard in the kitchen: Release this week, go. Under it someone has drawn a cat.
We closed the round. Dinner's on me tonight, order anything.
In the small meeting room you interview a kid fresh out of university. The CV says: Java, some Python.
I… I can learn. I really can.
You hired him. Later he called you Chief.
I can write SQL with my eyes shut. People who ask AI for everything, I don't rate them.
Whenever it was someone's birthday, the cake went from the meeting room all the way to the back row. Your slice was always just the cream.
Once this deal comes through, everyone gets paid this month.
You believed him. A dozen of the names on the payroll were people you had interviewed.
After that, every pivot, a few more desks went empty.
We're all in the same boat.
The last time in the office was an evening. The AI-native reform: the office was given up, everyone works from home.
No need to come in. I fought for that for you.
You pack your desk into a cardboard box.
Home. As if there were one.
